summary: Sporting News recaps the chaotic first half of Tottenham vs Chelsea on 6 November 2023, refereed by Michael Oliver with John Brooks on VAR. The half featured one red card, four yellows, four Chelsea goals ruled out and 12 minutes of stoppage time, ending 1-1 with Spurs down to 10 men. The article walks through each major VAR check and whether the decision was correct, while noting the lengthy reviews drew criticism.
one_line: A breakdown of every VAR intervention in a chaotic first half of Tottenham vs Chelsea, ending 1-1 with Romero sent off.
key_facts: Michael Oliver refereed Tottenham vs Chelsea with John Brooks as VAR official; the first half produced one red card and four yellow cards.
Chelsea had goals ruled out on four separate occasions in the first half, which led to 12 minutes of stoppage time.
The first half ended 1-1 with Tottenham reduced to 10 men.
Dejan Kulusevski opened the scoring for Spurs via a large deflection off Chelsea defender Levi Colwill, leaving Roberto Sanchez with no chance.
Heung-Min Son's apparent 2-0 goal in the 14th minute was disallowed after VAR showed him an inch offside.

Destiny Udogie got only a yellow card in the 18th minute for a two-footed tackle on Raheem Sterling because he missed and did not make full contact; Jon Champion said VAR judged it an "upper-level yellow card".
Cristian Romero kicked Levi Colwill in the calf in the 22nd minute without action, and VAR did not review it, likely because play had already restarted.
Raheem Sterling's 21st-minute equaliser was disallowed because a Pedro Porro block deflected the ball onto his arm, which is an automatic foul for an attacker.
In the 31st minute Moises Caicedo's goal was ruled out for offside against Nicolas Jackson, then Romero was sent off for a tackle on Raheem Sterling after a VAR review.
Cole Palmer scored the resulting penalty to make it 1-1.
Nicolas Jackson's goal in the 37th minute was disallowed because Raheem Sterling was offside in the buildup.
Reece James received only a yellow card for a trailing elbow to Destiny Udogie's face just before halftime, and VAR did not advise Oliver to check it.
